item.title: Waller, The Economic Outlook and Some Thoughts on Labor Market Dynamism

rating.summary: Governor Waller delivers a hawkish speech in London, noting that the U.S. economy is growing strongly and the labor market is near maximum employment, but inflation remains well above the 2% target. He signals support for a 25 basis point rate hike at the December FOMC meeting as a baseline, while leaving open the possibility of a 50 basis point hike if incoming CPI data disappoint. He also discusses structural concerns about declining labor market dynamism and its longer-run productivity implications.
rating.stance_rationale: Waller explicitly leans toward further tightening 'sooner rather than later,' commits to a 25bp December hike as his base case, and raises the prospect of a 50bp move if inflation data remain elevated—a clearly hawkish posture with an upside risk skew.
key_quotes: I believe further tightening of monetary policy will be needed, sooner rather than later, to return inflation to a path that will reach 2 percent in the medium term.

If the October CPI inflation data out later today are similar to the past two monthly readings—with core CPI inflation around 0.3 percent or even higher—then a stronger policy move may be needed. In that case, I believe a 50 basis point hike in the policy rate should be considered at the December meeting.
